title: tau doctor --json NDJSON event
description: Schema for one line of `tau doctor --json` output. With --json, doctor streams newline-delimited JSON: one check_event per diagnostic as it finishes, fix_event records interleaved when --fix runs, and exactly one terminal verdict_event (always the last line, always "done":true). The three event types are mutually exclusive — validate each NDJSON line against this schema individually. The single-object report printed without --json shares the check, fix, summary, and build object shapes below.

check_event.description: One diagnostic check result, emitted as the check finishes. Order is fixed by the check pipeline; every check appears exactly once per diagnosis pass (checks re-diagnosed after an applied --fix emit a second event with the post-fix outcome).

done.description: Stream-continuation marker — false on every non-terminal event.

check.name: api_key
check.hint: set XIAOMI_API_KEY or add keys.<provider> to config.json

fix_event.description: One remediation outcome, emitted only under `--fix` as each planned fix is approved, declined, skipped, or applied. Fix events appear between the first-pass check events and the verdict.

done.description: Stream-continuation marker — false on every non-terminal event.

verdict_event.description: Terminal verdict — always the last NDJSON line, always "done":true. Carries the whole-run outcome so a consumer reading only the last line gets the full verdict; the process exit code mirrors ok (0 when true, 1 when false).

ok.description: true when no check ended in fail status (warn/skip still count as passing).

version.description: tau version that produced the report, e.g. "0.4.0".

fixes.description: Present only when --fix ran — every remediation outcome in decision order.

done.description: End-of-stream marker — true on the verdict line only.

check.description: A single diagnostic outcome — the same object shape the single-object report carries in its "checks" array.

name.description: Stable machine name of the check, e.g. "config_file", "api_key", "endpoint_reachable".

status.description: Outcome of the check. warn counts toward ok:true; fail flips the verdict and the exit code to 1; skip means the check did not run (offline mode, missing prerequisite, or platform gating).

message.description: Human-readable result — what was found, never secret material.

hint.description: Optional remediation hint shown on non-ok outcomes.

fix.description: A remediation outcome — the same object shape the report and verdict carry in their "fixes" arrays.

id.description: Stable machine name of the remediation, e.g. "scaffold_config", "chmod_config", "install_completions".

check.description: Name of the check whose outcome triggered this fix.

status.description: What happened to the remediation. declined: the user answered no at the confirmation prompt; skipped: no approval channel (non-interactive run without --yes); failed: the fix was attempted and errored.

detail.description: Human-readable detail — what was done or why nothing was.

summary.description: Per-status tally over every check in the run.

warn.description: Checks that passed with a warning.

fail.description: Checks that failed — nonzero here forces ok:false and exit 1.

build.description: Build metadata identifying the exact binary — the same object `tau version --verbose` emits.

commit.description: Short git hash of HEAD at build time ("unknown" for tarball builds, "-dirty" suffix for uncommitted changes).

build_date.description: UTC build stamp YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH honored for reproducible builds).

zig.description: Zig compiler version that produced the binary, e.g. "0.16.0".
